screens.name: Bridport South Road
screens.note: East and south into Shoreham's north orchards.
screens.quiet: East and south into Shoreham's north orchards.

interactions.text: East and south into Shoreham's north orchards.

hubs.name: Middlebury village green
hubs.blurb: Green and merchant row of the shire town. The Ledger Key is in records.

hubs.name: College terrace quad
hubs.blurb: A quad above the river. Not a full campus map.

hubs.name: Vergennes falls green
hubs.blurb: City green beside Otter Creek Falls.

hubs.name: Bristol park
hubs.blurb: Village park and the buildings on it.

hubs.name: Basin Harbor green
hubs.blurb: Harbor green. Masts, not a menu.

hubs.name: Dunmore landing
hubs.blurb: Landing on Lake Dunmore, in Salisbury.

hubs.name: Bread Loaf meadow
hubs.blurb: Meadow west of Middlebury Gap. A compressed public green.

hubs.name: Lincoln corner
hubs.blurb: General, meeting room, and kitchen at the village corner.

hubs.name: Shoreham creamery square
hubs.blurb: Creamery square. Year 42 moves loading talk to the east door, outside.

hubs.name: Orwell common
hubs.blurb: Southern common. The county ends south of the farms, not here.

interiors.name: Stone Mill Inn room
interiors.purpose: The bed is made in a name Ellis has already died out of.

interiors.name: Otter bakery
interiors.purpose: The ovens are warm. Nothing is for sale; this is not a shop economy.

interiors.name: Green bookstore
interiors.purpose: Shelves face the green. One spine is blank every time Ellis returns.

interiors.name: South-street tavern
interiors.purpose: The bar keeps a stool empty without calling it a shrine.

interiors.name: Shire records
interiors.purpose: The Ledger Key is in the open minute-book. It opens civic doors, not a shop.

interiors.name: Library stair
interiors.purpose: A public stair, not a staff office. The lower door is the stacks mouth outside.

interiors.name: Chapel nave
interiors.purpose: Benches and a quiet that does not ask you to pray.

interiors.name: Dorm hall
interiors.purpose: Closed doors along a hall. You do not enter the rooms. The hall itself is the interior.

interiors.name: Falls stair
interiors.purpose: Spray on the steps under the footbridge. A place to stand, not a shortcut.

interiors.name: Bridge watch
interiors.purpose: A fictional watch room on the Middlebury bank of the Pulp Mill bridge.

interiors.name: Knoll observatory
interiors.purpose: A small dome on the construction hill. The warp of year 70 is outside, on the grass.

interiors.name: City clerk
interiors.purpose: Counter, bell, a clock that gains fourteen years when you look away.

interiors.name: Shipyard loft
interiors.purpose: Fictional loft above the landing. The city's shipyard years are the subject, not a copied museum.

interiors.name: Falls cafe
interiors.purpose: Two tables and the sound of the falls through the wall.

interiors.name: Catwalk booth
interiors.purpose: A booth that looks at the race. After year 56 the window shows a gap.

interiors.name: Mill office
interiors.purpose: Ledgers of water, not of money you can spend.

interiors.name: City boathouse
interiors.purpose: Oars on pegs that are not the Void Oar. Creek Boots are not here.

interiors.name: Park cafe
interiors.purpose: Counter toward the park. You can sit. You cannot buy a craft.

interiors.name: Town hall lobby
interiors.purpose: A lobby and a closed meeting door. The lobby is as far as the building goes.

interiors.name: Pottery showroom
interiors.purpose: Shelves of bowls. They are not components.

interiors.name: Bristol general
interiors.purpose: Aisles you can walk. Nothing transfers into an inventory economy.

interiors.name: Bartlett shelter
interiors.purpose: Three walls and a view of the gorge. The line is cached on the rim, not in here.

interiors.name: Junction depot
interiors.purpose: Benches and a board. In year 56 the board is blank.

interiors.name: New Haven mill floor
interiors.purpose: The stone is still. Flour smell, no wheel.

interiors.name: Harbor inn taproom
interiors.purpose: A low room, lake light, no quest board.

interiors.name: Ferrisburgh general
interiors.purpose: Nails, rope, and nothing you combine.

interiors.name: Basin farm kitchen
interiors.purpose: A kitchen that feeds the people who live there. You may stand in it.

interiors.name: Marsh boatshed
interiors.purpose: Creek Boots hang on a peg above the dry floor, off the rotten boardwalk.

interiors.name: Marsh blind
interiors.purpose: A wildlife blind. The slot frames reeds. An encounter does not live here; the thicket does.

interiors.name: Landing store
interiors.purpose: Bait coolers and a bell. Not a market system.

interiors.name: Lake meeting room
interiors.purpose: Folding chairs and a map of the shore that does not include the glass.

interiors.name: Dunmore boathouse
interiors.purpose: The keeper is present until year 70, then absent. The door still opens.

interiors.name: West cabin
interiors.purpose: A cabin above the road that does not flood. The shore below does.

interiors.name: Cove glass chapel
interiors.purpose: Fictional. Glass in the walls shows the year you are not in.

interiors.name: Ripton inn
interiors.purpose: A small inn room off the meadow, west of the gap.

interiors.name: Meadow barn classroom
interiors.purpose: Benches in a barn. It is not a copy of a campus interior.

interiors.name: Notch cabin
interiors.purpose: Frost Notch hangs by the door, on the village side of the windwall.

interiors.name: Falls road shelter
interiors.purpose: A shelter west of the windwall, before Texas Falls.

interiors.name: Hancock store
interiors.purpose: A counter east of the gap. You only reach it through the windwall.

interiors.name: Lincoln general
interiors.purpose: The corner store. The warp is outside.

interiors.name: Lincoln meeting room
interiors.purpose: Benches and a stove. Town business you can overhear and not join.

interiors.name: Farm kitchen
interiors.purpose: A kitchen behind the general. Bread, not a recipe system.

interiors.name: Sugarhouse
interiors.purpose: The Sugar Tap is on the evaporator. The lane is north of the washout.

interiors.name: Flume shed
interiors.purpose: Tools for the flume. The dungeon mouth is outside, on the walk.

interiors.name: Creamery floor
interiors.purpose: Vats and a board. Year 42 the board lists members instead of hours.

interiors.name: Orchard church hall
interiors.purpose: A hall, not a dungeon. Hymnals that do not mention the void.

interiors.name: Packing barn
interiors.purpose: The Orchard Ladder is on the north wall, above crates that are not loot.

interiors.name: Orchard house
interiors.purpose: A kitchen window onto rows. The rows are the puzzle, outside.

interiors.name: Point cottage
interiors.purpose: A cottage at Larrabee's Point. The far shore is not a door.

interiors.name: Common tavern
interiors.purpose: A bar toward the common. The empty stool is a habit, not a quest.

interiors.name: Orwell hall
interiors.purpose: A hall with a map that stops at the county line.

interiors.name: South farmhouse
interiors.purpose: Mud room and table. The bluff is outside.

interiors.name: Independence shed
interiors.purpose: A fictional shed at the historic gate. It does not reproduce a museum. The tunnels open in year 56, outside.

interiors.name: Creek barn
interiors.purpose: A barn on the way back up from the one-way bluff.

interiors.name: Lime office
interiors.purpose: A desk of weigh tickets. The lamp is outside on the yard table.

interiors.name: Morgan gate tack shed
interiors.purpose: Fictional shed at the farm gate. The working barns are not entered.

interiors.name: Pulp Mill watch
interiors.purpose: The Weybridge side of the covered bridge. You can hear traffic until year 56, then hammers.

interiors.name: Cut shack
interiors.purpose: A shack at the dark cut. The lamp is next door in the kiln yard, not locked in here.

interiors.name: Goose blind
interiors.purpose: A blind on the flats. Quiet is the use of the screen.

interiors.name: Chimney Point keeper cottage
interiors.purpose: The Void Oar is on the table. The bridge outside leaves the county and is not a path.

eraChanges.summary: Little Otter boardwalk between the harbor green and the gauge rots. Creek Boots cross it. The village road to the east stays a road.
The cedar trail from Kingsland Cedars south to the thicket is closed. Traffic uses the marsh dike instead.
Button Bay dock sinks. The cistern mouth, previously Creek Boots on the shore, now wants the Void Oar.
The Monkton ridge span opens, a road from Monkton Ridge Foot to West Bristol Fields that skips New Haven.
The mill-race crossing from the overlook to the race opens. It is shut in year 0.
The race is fenced again and the underworks mouth is buried. North Main and Creek Road still cross town.
The race fence comes down on the east bank. The underworks mouth is open again. Crossing is a road until the catwalk fails in year 56.
The falls catwalk collapses. East-west across the overlook wants the Falls Line. North-south streets stay open.
A glass weir at Belden Falls opens a Creek Boots span from the New Haven rim to the Vergennes falls foot.

interaction.text: The south flats have dried to pasture. The road was never the wet part.

eraChanges.summary: The Otter meander crossing into Ferrisburgh goes deep and wants the Void Oar. The crossings north and south of it stay dry.
The fence at New Haven Junction comes down. The siding is a south shortcut that did not exist in earlier years.
The north field cross between the elm and Brooksville hedge closes. Go south, then east. The depot board goes blank.

interaction.text: The junction board is a blank timetable. Nobody is staffing the depot.

eraChanges.summary: Washouts make two one-way descents: Rocky Dale down to the switchback, and Bartlett Throat down to the village east. Climb back on the long roads.
A landslide closes East Woods Corner into Lincoln's river road. Notch Road West, the valley road, still reaches West Lincoln.
The Deer Leap switchback east closes. A new climb north to South Starksboro wants Ledge Iron.
A void seam at the New Haven River bend reaches the Lincoln gap vista. Frost Notch or the Void Oar will do. The vista still does not enter Warren.
The sugar flume opens as a Sugar Tap shortcut from the village west down to the flume walk. The valley road is still open.
The valley road and both side paths between the village row and South Lincoln wash out. Only the flume, with the Sugar Tap, reaches the south slopes.
The Void Oar can reach the gap vista from the Ripton windwall. Frost Notch still parts the windwall itself. Warren stays sealed.
The village roads are rebuilt, so the south slopes no longer need the Sugar Tap. The flume itself rots. The dungeon under the flume remains, reached from the restored south roads.
Construction closes College Hill Road's east cut. Mill Street, one screen south, is the detour.

interaction.text: The foreman will not let you up the gravel. The street below is still a street.

eraChanges.summary: The falls footbridge's north span wants the Falls Line through year 41. Mill Street goes around.
The footbridge is rebuilt and no longer wants the line. Printer's Alley, west into the bridge screen, now wants the Ledger Key.
The Pulp Mill bridge and the two ledge roads beside it close for restoration. The Cornwall north lane stays open as the detour.
The return bank's south path becomes a void seam and wants the Void Oar. Other south roads into Salisbury stay. A new glass-warp roots on the college knoll.
The wayside's south leg grows shut. Enter from the hollow or the plains and leave the way you came.
Bread Loaf's north pasture gate locks. Reach the meadow from Route 125, not from the upper plains.
The windwall still wants Frost Notch, but the Void Oar now parts it too. Hancock and Texas Falls stay east of that line.
The Granville gulf culvert drops, cutting the road from Hancock. The trail from Texas Falls wants Creek Boots. The spiral mouth behind the falls opens and wants the Falls Line.
Dunmore's west shore floods deep. Every exit wants the Void Oar. Lake Road, the Leicester river, and the east cove go around it.
The Falls of Lana footbridge wants the Falls Line. Both rims remain reachable without crossing.
The Leicester Junction rail bed, rubble until now, opens east as a shortcut along the lake.
The glass-warp leaves the shard shore and re-roots at the east cove. The old pad is dead. You do not keep the new one until you stand on it.

interaction.text: The landing keeper is gone. The boathouse door sticks and then gives. Nothing inside has been updated.

eraChanges.summary: Orchard walls become trellises. The north wall wants the Orchard Ladder. The old hedge footpath closes. Center road stays a road.
The creamery loading talk moves from the south apron to the east door. The hub is the same building. The cooperative board replaces the open office.

interaction.text: Loading happens at the east door now. The south apron is just apron. The board inside lists members, not hours.

eraChanges.summary: Larrabee's wharf stair collapses into deep water and wants the Void Oar. Cove Stones is the shore path around it. The point does not become a ferry to New York.
The oldest orchard's east hedge opens a new road onto Mount Independence's gate screen. A glass-warp roots among the old trees.
A farm hedge closes the middle of Orwell's north street unless you have the Orchard Ladder. North Farm to 22A to the village goes around.
The bluff path becomes one-way down toward the south county seal. Climb back through Creek Farm and the south farms.
The void bay seam opens for the Void Oar, a loop that stays inside Orwell. Mount Independence's fictional tunnels open the same year.
A ledge path from the south farms into the void bay wants Ledge Iron, so the bay is no longer only an oar screen.
A cut collapses open between the dark cut and Cornwall's north lane. It wants the Quarry Lamp. The lime-kiln road to the west stays in the light.
The Lemon Fair floods every north-south crossing in the Cornwall-Whiting block. Without the oar, go around through Salisbury, Shoreham, or Orwell.
The flooded pit's rim collapses. West, east, and south joins want the Void Oar. The pit screen is oar-only. Neighbors still connect around it.
The Dead Creek bridge's north span closes. The detour is east to Addison flats, then back.
The goose-flats dike opens east, a wet shortcut that wants Creek Boots. Before this year the dike is not a path.
With the Void Oar from Chimney Point, a water span skips the broken Dead Creek bridge.
A void seam under the Crown Point approach runs north along the Vermont shore to Snake Mountain's foot. It does not cross into New York.
